messages.text: I can drop the casserole by your place in Van Buren after work. Should I make the smaller pan?
Smaller is plenty. We will get two suppers out of it and maybe one lunch if I do not sneak seconds.
I'll leave it on the porch table if y'all are still out. No need to move anything inside for me.
Thanks. The porch is clear except the plant stand, and she already washed the two glass dishes.
Maddie asked if she could bring her sketchbook by after parish supper Friday. She liked how you talked through shading last time.
Sure. The back room is clear except for my watercolor bins, so she and Cole can spread out at the table.
Thanks. I figured your place would be quieter than mine that evening.
It will just be the two of us until they arrive. I will make chili and keep the front porch light on.
Mama asked if you were still looking at that Fort Smith office thing.
I told them I am keeping my name out of anything with daily desk hours or a commute right now.
That sounds more like you. The Van Buren arts people still need someone to keep sign-up sheets straight, don't they?
Yes. Two mornings and some calls from home is the shape I can actually keep alongside supper and Sunday visits.
Before you call back this morning, check the blue folder. The tooth place estimate and Dr. P's invoice are both in there.
I saw them. I can do one this paycheck, not both.
Then ask both offices what the smallest down payment is. Don't just let the dates slide off the calendar.
I'll call after coffee and write the numbers beside the March bills.
Before I go by Harps, do you want me to wait until Friday for the bigger shop?
Yes. I can make the beans, rice, and that half bag of pasta stretch two more nights.
Good. Also the porch latch is sticking again if you have ten minutes after supper.
I'll look at it after I water the tomatoes. No need to buy anything for it yet.
If we go to Eureka Springs Saturday, let's keep it to lunch and the 2:00 fiddle set. Back before dark.
That sounds about right. I also tucked those Plaza vendor photos into the Santa Fe folder after supper.
Good. One folder at a time, one Saturday at a time.
Could you bring the sign-up sheet Thursday and sit by me for the first few minutes? People ask fewer nervous questions when you explain the flow.
I can do that. I still feel like I'm borrowing your confidence on these evenings.
Borrow it if you need, but the room responds because you keep things kind and practical.
I'll print 20 sheets and mark the beginner table in blue tape.
Can you bring the March watercolor sign-in pages Thursday? I only have the old winter ones.
Yes. I will print 35 blanks and add the supply column before I come by.
Thank you. Also, Linda and Curtis both want the front wall for their pieces, so we may need your calm voice there.
I can talk them through the wall layout after I check the tables and water cups.
Could you still help set up folding chairs before the Friday supper? The choir folders are stacked in the hall closet.
Yes. I'll come straight after work, but let's keep it simple and use the tables already downstairs.
Good. Your mother's alto part always steadied that room. I still hear it when the old green book comes out.
I remember standing beside her and trying to follow the page numbers. I'll bring the tape and name tags.
Evan, that square picture you put up from the parish fish supper had the courthouse lights in the back. Very pretty.
Thank you. I stepped outside before cleanup and caught the wet street shining a little.
Was that on Instagram? My niece showed me where to tap the heart.
Yes ma'am. I may add one from the river walk if the light holds after work.
Did you see the end of that Fayetteville game? My grandson hollered so loud I heard him from the kitchen.
I saw it. I typed one little Woo Pig under Tom's post and now three people are still going back and forth on my page.
You always find the lively bunch online after a close one.
It is mostly harmless. I will hush before supper gets cold.
You still okay for Saturday? I saw the ridge route and thought about our knees.
Yes, but let's keep it to the shorter loop. My body keeps reminding me Van Buren '95 was a while back.
Fair. Bring poles. Also, did you finish that online form for the volunteer badge?
Almost. It keeps asking for the last place I finished anything, so I used Van Buren and 1995 again.
Mom said Uncle Ray might come by after parish setup Sunday. Can you bring the beans again?
Yes. I'll start them Saturday night and bring the big pot.
Good. Cousin Lisa asked if you'd save her a bowl before the boys get to it.
I'll set one aside and call Dad tomorrow to make sure he still wants cornbread.
I can take Mom by Harps Friday if you need that library class slot.
Thanks. It is the one with the practice cards and role-play. I want to learn how to sit steady with somebody before they spin out.
You always remember what helped and what made it worse. That will matter.
That is the hope. Same idea for the studio table: clear instructions, no judging, coffee already made.
Before you answer your cousin, check the Arkansas page and ask Carla at the pharmacy when you pick up milk.
Before you send the lodge form, make sure they put us in the quiet wing again.
Good call. That screenshot she sent has no date on it anyway.
Already checked that box and added the note about keeping the room away from the late porch crowd.
Good. Last year you came back from that porch with your jacket airing out on the laundry door.
Just send her the link after breakfast. No need to argue in the comments.
I'll look at the CDC table too and keep it short.
I remember. This time I'll just bring coffee inside and skip whatever they pass around out there.
That event post at the King Opera House says two seats would be $52 before fees.
Let's hold off unless they drop a cheaper door price. I still want to hear that fiddle player sometime.
Agreed. I saved the post so we can check again Friday after bills clear.
The reel with the blue-gray wash made me think of your backdrop flats.
I saved it. Might try that look before I haul the props bin over Thursday.
Good. And the bridge photo you sent has the right mood for that last scene.
I'll bring the printed copy with my script pages so I don't forget.
The supply order is still short two paper packs. If setup runs late tomorrow, do you want me to bring something small before the room opens?
Maybe crackers or an apple. If I leave hungry after a messy setup, I keep thinking about the fried catfish basket at Catfish Hole.
I can put a snack bag by the sign-in sheets. Keeps you from making supper decisions in the parking lot.
Good. Last workshop week that parking lot decision somehow included extra bacon on the side.
Evan, are you still coming by before the Friday supper to set out the long tables?
Yes. I can stop after I drop the garden flats at the side room.
Good. Mary said the same room is being used for the small paintings on Saturday.
I'll leave the back wall clear and call Mrs. Delaney after lunch.
Evan, some folks are talking about carrying signs by the courthouse Friday. Are you going over there?
For Saturday's supper table, are you bringing that red sauce your family makes?
I don't think so. If Harold brings it up at the fish supper, I may just ask him what he meant and tell him about the Ortiz boys from catechism.
Yes. I'll start it Friday night and bring it over after I swing through downtown Fort Smith for the pans.
That sounds more like you. People listen better when you keep it plain.
Good. Put me by the folks who remember your grandparents' old Sunday table stories.
Plain is about all I can manage. One question, one real example, then let the table breathe.
I'll do that. Half the room will know the Van Buren side before I even set the pot down.
Saturday loop has that long rocky drop after the overlook. Want me to bring the extra pair of poles just in case?
I'll pack mine. Also switching back to the brown boots after last week.
Good call. I'll toss in the peanut bars and keep us off the slick creek crossing if it rains.
Works. I need five minutes at the trailhead before we start, then I'm fine.
Before you answer Mary, check the kitchen calendar. You already have the 1:30 grocery run and the parish call after that.
I saw it. I am keeping the creek sketch first, then I will text her after breakfast.
Good. One thing at a time this morning, then the practical stuff this afternoon.
That layout worked better yesterday. I did not chase three things before 9.
The bluegrass show still has two seats, but they are higher than last time.
Let's leave those alone tonight. I want to see where the washer part lands first.
Works for me. The library room has that free folk set at 7 if you still want music.
That sounds better. We can keep the little Bentonville idea penciled in for another weekend.
Yesterday went smoother because you kept the supply table moving. I barely had to leave the easels.
Glad it helped. The two new folks looked less lost once the water cups and scrap sheets were already out.
Exactly. Can I put you down for the same clipboard-and-room flow on the 19th?
Yes. I will check the closet first so nobody is hunting for tape while paint is drying.
Can you look at the display table map before Thursday? I don't want another scramble over who gets the front corner.
I can, but I need to run tonight's calendar with my wife first. If Tuesday is open, I'll clean up the map and the intake sheet.
That works. The one-page sheet you mentioned would help, especially the part about labels and drop-off times.
I'll send a plain version after supper if the evening isn't already spoken for.
Are you still taking those sample sheets by the parish hall after coffee?
Yes. I printed a few extras, mostly the city and county pages.
Good. I get lost when the little offices are all mixed together.
Same here, so I mark notes ahead. It feels like one of those things neighbors ought to help each other sort through.
Lee Creek still looks dry enough. You bringing the poles or trusting that knee?
Poles are already by the back door. I'll keep the pace sensible this time.
Good. Randy said wheels roll from the courthouse lot at 6:45.
I'll be there with coffee and those peanut crackers you steal every time.
Mom asked if you were still going by the clinic before the parish lunch.
Yes. Dr. Harris's nurse said they can look at my card and tell me what I am due for.
Good. Bring your reading glasses this time so you don't have to call me from the lobby.
Fair. I put the card in my wallet already.
The bank draft cleared this morning. I put the escrow letter beside the coffee tin so we can look at it after supper.
Thanks. I'll check the mower gas after lunch and trim around the azaleas by the front steps.
Good. Also please get the canvas roll off the guest bed before your sister comes tomorrow.
I'll stack it with the tubes and brushes in the back room.
Lunch was good. You two still doing the Sunday roast next time?
Yes, if the week stays reasonable. I told her I would check the house calendar first.
Smart. She has always been better than the rest of us at spotting when your plate is too full.
That is why I wait before I say yes.
Do you still want to bring rolls tomorrow, or should I cover them?
Can you cover them? I keep adding little things to tomorrow's list and my chest is doing that tight thing.
I'll get the rolls. Go shut the notebook and get some sleep.
Thanks. I was about two minutes from calling the whole visit off, which is silly because I do want to see everybody.
Before supper, can you grab the church donation slips from the green folder?
I have them. I also wrote the mileage total on the back page of the notebook.
Good. After dishes I'll open the return program and see if it pulls last year's numbers cleanly.
I'll sit with you and read off the totals instead of guessing from the drawer pile.
Can you bring extra clipboards Tuesday? Last month the same three names took the front wall before anyone else arrived.
Yes. I will put sign-up sheets on both tables and leave the first row open until 6:20.
Good. Also, maybe one sentence beside each piece? The porch-flood paintings need more than a title.
I will bring 3x5 cards and ask people what they want written, not write it for them.
I saw your post about Tuesday soup. I can bring crackers if someone can lift the box from my trunk.
That helps. I will add it under the St. Michael's note and ask Randy to meet you by the side door.
Thank you. Folks were still talking by the cars about the library tax sheet, so I may wait inside after Mass.
Good plan. I will keep the meal list simple and leave the tax sheet talk for after coffee.
Can you take Dad to Fort Smith Tuesday morning, or are you tied up?
I can take him. My calendar is open before the arts council room setup.
Thanks. I know you and her are watching March expenses, so I'll cover gas and lunch.
That helps. We're trying to stretch what landed Friday until the utilities clear.
Aunt Linda said the crowd on Main had drums and posters again. Mom wondered if you were in the middle of it.
No, I was at the parish hall stacking chairs. I did talk to Kenny afterward about what he said at supper.
Please tell me you didn't let him bait you.
I asked him if he'd say the same thing after meeting Teresa's grandkids, then I told him how they helped Dad with the ramp.
Are you still going by the council desk tonight? I wrote down that the crosswalk by the school feels quick.
Yes. I can mention that and the clinic bus stop bench. I also want the complaint cards kept at the front desk, not tucked behind the counter.
Thank you. Plain forms where people can see them would help.
I'll keep it practical. Sidewalk, bench, forms, and who reviews them.
Thank you for the ride Thursday. Could we go the road by the levee again if it is not out of your way?
That works. I like that stretch before lunch, and I can bring the small paper pad if we have a few minutes.
My tomato starts are in the window now. The birds have found the feeder too.
Good. I will come a little early so I can see both before we leave.
Before you answer Mary, go take your block loop and water the tomato starts.
Long meeting finally over?
Doing that now. I will look at the calendar after I get dirt under my nails.
Just got home. I'm going to walk the block twice before supper.
Good. Also remember those folding tables are heavier than they look, so don't promise a second room setup tonight.
Good. I saved you tea and the leftover chicken.
Perfect. No need to open anything special tonight.
Back inside. The walk helped me quit clenching my jaw, and the tomatoes are soaked.
Before you answer Mary, look at Thursday and Saturday both. You already have parish setup after supper.
I know. The arts room needs a steady hand that night, but I can leave by 7 if I pack the brush bins first.
Then tell them the exact time you can do. You do better when the promise is clear.
Fair. I will say setup and first half only, and I will not add the display boards too.
I'm tempted to pull out of the display meeting. Tim says Sandra promised him the first panel, and Sandra says she never did.
Don't answer while you're keyed up. Call each of them tomorrow, write down the dates they mention, then decide what the sheet needs to say.
Fair. I'll make the calls before I change the table chart.
And check our Friday first. You already have parish setup penciled in.
Did you see the Crawford County page shared a Saturday porch-stage thing by the market?
Yes, I tapped interested so it stays where I can find it. Looks like mandolin and harmony singers.
Sounds like your kind of night if the tickets don't get silly.
Exactly. I'll ask her tonight if we can make the numbers work.
Sunday lunch still at your place? If it stays mild, Mom would rather sit out front than inside.
Yes. I'll wipe down the porch chairs and clear the seed trays off the rail.
Want me to bring that folder from First National? You said the payment schedule changed.
Please do. I need to compare it with the March draft before I file it.
Mom asked if you ever got that cracked back tooth handled.
Not yet. They quoted more than I planned, so I moved it behind the truck tag and utilities.
Don't let it turn into Sunday soup-only meals again. Also did you keep your Tuesday hour with Dr. P?
I pushed that too. Same reason, different office.
Before you answer Mary, count the hours already on the fridge calendar.
I have Monday receipts, Thursday setup, and Saturday morning check-in table. Looks like 11 before any extra calls.
Then only say yes to the speaker intro if someone else handles the coffee order.
Fair. I will ask Sam to take coffee and keep me to the intro plus the sheets.
Mary left that packet by the door. Is that for tonight's council room layout?
Yes. She marked where she wants the display boards, and somehow my name is on the welcome table again.
Then eat before you go and keep the list short. Also, you sounded steadier after her call yesterday.
She has a way of making the whole thing feel like I belong at the table, not just carrying boxes.
Did you already answer about Saturday, or are you waiting until after you check the cue sheet?
Waiting. I still need to mark the lamp cue, then I have two pages to say with Linda.
I saw you saved three costume photos at supper. Pick one jacket idea and be done.
Fair. The brown one matches the room photo I sent Mary, so I'll stop scrolling.
Do you want me to bring extra cold-press paper Saturday, or are you set after your hill studies this week?
Bring one pad if you have it. I used more than I meant to before the phone started ringing.
I like that you are guarding that early slot. The workshop list can wait until after lunch.
Could you sit with the high-school volunteers at the registration table Saturday? They listened to you better than they listened to me last month.
I can. My wife and I have a clear morning, and I already have the name tags in the truck.
Perfect. If Jonah freezes again, let him do the brush rinsing first and ease in.
That worked last time. I will bring the small watercolor pads too.
Are you still going to Little Rock for that Saturday exhibit?
Probably not this round. The gutter quote came in and I am keeping the card quiet.
Then come help hang the depot pieces Friday. No fee, and I can bring extra clips.
I can do that. I will skip buying paper this week and use what is in the flat file.
I found the book with the Canyon Road doorway sketches. Want me to bring it to the workshop table?
Please do. I keep comparing those colors with the Pueblo market photos I saved.
Then you and your wife need a little practice run somewhere closer this month. Tulsa has that evening folk bill on the 21st.
I'll ask her tonight. A close one is easier than trying to make the big folder happen all at once.
For Saturday's watercolor room, can you bring the folding table, blue tape, and those rubber floor mats?
Yes. I'll wear the work boots and bring the poles from the truck too, since the back ramp is steep with boxes.
Thank you. I'll have two students carry the water jugs so you can handle signs and tape.
Perfect. Give me a few minutes after unloading before we start hanging paper.
Can you bring the blue tape and the extra sign-up sheet for the watercolor room?
Yes. I also have the name cards from the theater lobby box.
Perfect. If you see Mr. Ortiz at supper tomorrow, ask whether he wants a ride to the opening.
I can ask him when I take the coffee urn back.
I sent you two IG accounts that handle fog on hills beautifully. One of them paints the Buffalo River bend almost too neatly.
I saved both. The second one has the kind of green wash I keep trying to get for the Ozark ridge behind town.
Bring that ridge snapshot Saturday if you still have it. It might help the beginners see where the shadows go.
I'll print the less muddy one. There was a hawk sitting on the fence line, so I kept the frame wider.
If we start at 7 Saturday, you will be back before the noon tip?
That works. I already told the group page I would be quiet on the trail and noisy after the final.
Bring poles then. That climb is easier if you are not checking score comments every bend.
Fair. I will leave the score fuss for the parking lot.
Saturday loop still 8:00? Trail report says mud by the creek.
8 works. If I don't get to the courthouse Friday, remind me to leave by 2 Tuesday before the lines get long.
You and your errands. Bring poles if we do the west side.
Will do. I still need to read up on those county names before I mark anything.
Do you still keep medical receipts in that folder? Mom asked what you do with hers.
Yes, folder first, then I total them in the notebook when we sit down together.
That sounds like you. Do you mail anything now or just send it from the computer?
Mostly send it from the computer once my wife checks the numbers against the bank screen.
For Sunday, Mama asked whether you want ribs or chicken. She still has cornmeal from last time.
Chicken is safer if the parish signup mess follows me into Sunday. If ribs and cornbread are sitting there, I make a second lap before I notice.
I'll tell her chicken, green beans, and one small skillet of cornbread. You can take a plate home instead of hovering by the stove.
That would help. Same reason I'm skipping bacon in the beans this week.
Do you want me to bring Mom's potato soup tonight, or are you doing the fish line first?
I'll do the fish line and then meet you downstairs. No need to buy extra rolls; we have enough from last week.
I found Dad's little songbook in the cedar chest. It has your pencil marks all over the refrain pages.
Save it for me. Those pages got me through a lot of long Fridays when we were kids.
I found the school scrapbook with the old Van Buren class photos. Want it Sunday?
Yes, bring it. I can put it beside the hospital bracelet envelope so the cousins stop arguing about where things started.
Also, the volunteer form asked the same two background questions as last year. I left yours the way you always mark it: no on the first one, then the box with the European examples.
That matches mine. Thanks for handling it before the parish office closes.
My deposit posted. Please move $90 to groceries and leave the rest for electric.
Done. I held off on the new brushes and marked the workshop supplies as donated only.
Good. Also, do not say yes to another committee dinner until we look at the month.
Agreed. I have time, but the gas and meals add up fast.
I moved the grocery pickup to 12:30 so your morning group won't make us rush.
Thanks. Their route is shorter than last time, so I should be home before lunch.
Please take the blue bottle and don't come back limping like after Devil's Den.
Fair. Boots are cleaned and the pack is by the washer.
I talked with Elaine. She can write it as 10 to 12 hours most weeks, mostly mornings, with the rest by phone.
That is the only version I should put my name beside. I can keep beginners, supplies, and reminder calls moving at that pace.
Good. I also told her you weren't the person for a big regional rollout.
Thank you. Let me do the Van Buren room well before anyone starts adding counties.
Evan, I found that old photo from the 1987 parish supper. Do you still want a copy for the table at the art room?
Yes, please. A copy is perfect. I can set it beside the painted plates if you are comfortable with that.
That is fine. My handwriting is shaky, but I can tell you who is in it.
Could you still come by after the noon Mass? The little shelf by my phone is loose.
I can bring a card and write only the names and the supper note you give me.
I can. I'll bring a screwdriver and a container of soup from last night's pot.
You don't need to fuss over food.
It's already made. We were keeping supper simple until the check clears.
I got that notice from the drugstore and do not know if I should fool with it.
I would call your own doctor's office first. That is what I do when those notices come.
Could you remind me of the clinic number after supper?
Yes. Mine is on Towson, but I will find yours before I call.
Carpool Saturday? Rick said his cooler is full and he may hang back at the overlook awhile.
I'll drive my truck if we keep it just water, coffee, and trail snacks.
Works for me. I'll tell Rick to ride with Dale if he wants the overlook stop.
Thanks. I don't want my cab smelling odd before church setup Sunday.
Mom found your old senior picture sleeve while cleaning the hall closet.
The one with the green backdrop? I thought that disappeared before the reunion mailer came last fall.
Same one. She also found the program from your '95 ceremony, if you want it.
Save it for Sunday. I need the date off it for another application box anyway.
Before we buy groceries, are we doing your sister's place tomorrow or your parents'?
Sister's this time. Dad wants me to call him tonight, and Aunt Linda asked about chicken and rice.
Then get the big foil pans. I'll grab rolls and tea while you check the freezer.
Thanks. I'll make enough so we can leave a couple plates behind.
For the workshop table, do you want me to save space for those blue-gray wash samples?
Yes, especially the ones from the bend below the bridge. The shadow shapes finally behaved.
Bring the ridge studies too. Beginners will understand the layers if they can see them side by side.
I will. I may stop by the water first if the late light is clear.
Evan, thank you for calling Mrs. Larkin yesterday. She said you did not rush her.
I just kept my voice low and let her get the words out. That is one of the things I am trying to practice before the Saturday course.
That gentle way would help at the church painting afternoon too. Some folks will come only if they know nobody will fuss over mistakes.
I will set out scrap sheets first so nobody has to start on the good paper.
Still meeting at 7:20 by the lot? Forecast looks dry.
I'm up. Slept rough and my brain already has twelve errands stacked behind the hike.
Easy loop then. Bring poles if you want, and we can skip the coffee crowd after.
That helps. I almost bailed, but the easy loop sounds manageable.
Still meeting at 8:15, or did the arts meeting run you ragged?
I am coming. Sat on the porch with coffee after supper and got talked down from adding one more thing.
Still on for the short ridge route? Mud at the first crossing, but nothing too wild.
Good call. Bring poles if your knee is still touchy from Lee Creek.
Yes. I loaded poles and a banana. Need to be back by 10:30 so I can turn the compost before the arts room setup.
Sounds like a full morning. I will keep us moving but not racing.
You still bringing that cooler for after the hike?
Yep. Water, oranges, and two root beers. I left the cookout bottles at home.
Fine by me. My knees just want shade by noon.
Trailhead at 9 still work? I can swing by your house if your knee wants the shorter ride.
Meet there is fine. She is sleeping in, so I am leaving the house quiet.
Got it. Bring poles if you want; mud was bad by the creek.
Packed them by the door last night with one snack bag for me and one coffee mug rinsed for when I get back.
You make it to the river access meeting after the hike or did your knee vote no?
Made it. They talked parking, trash cans, and whether the gate stays open past 7. I asked if the patrol log can show when cameras are actually checked.
That sounds more useful than another sign nobody reads.
Exactly. Also slipped in a plug for Saturday buses to the clinic and the library.
Your note on the trail thread got three maybes. Lee says the creek is high at Shores Lake.
I will update it after supper. If we switch to Lake Fort Smith, I will pin the 8:30 meetup.
Fine by me. Same thread had Tommy fussing about the county road plan again.
I saw that. I will keep tomorrow's post to boots, water, and the shorter loop.
Evan, someone at lunch showed me a post saying not to get the spring clinic shot. I got worried.
I'll bring the Arkansas Department of Health printout by after Mass. It has the clinic dates and who they say should ask first.
Thank you. Could you also ask the lady at your pharmacy? She explained my last one plainly.
Yes. I am stopping there Monday and will write down what she says.
Mom asked if you already handled your courthouse stop or if you are going after work.
After work today. I missed my clean window last week.
She also said don't just follow Dad's cheat sheet for mayor.
I won't. The city stuff needs its own look, even when the top lines are easy.
Aunt Linda said your red-hat post after the game made Uncle Ray start texting in all caps.
He started it with that missed-call complaint. I only put up the box score and one sentence.
One sentence from you after a close Fayetteville finish is bait and you know it.
I checked the comments twice, then shut it down. Tell Aunt Linda I am behaving.
Before you say yes to Saturday, check the grocery total. We planned $85 and the pantry is fine.
I won't add another supply run. I can help carry boxes after the noon rehearsal and use what they already have.
Good. Also, your sister asked whether you're taking the worn blue book tomorrow for the nieces.
Yes. If they sit with us, they can follow the responses instead of fidgeting through the music.
Before you say yes to Sunday, remember we already have Caleb's confirmation practice pickup at 3:00.
Right. I can take Caleb, drop him at St. Michael's, then be home before supper.
That works. We do not need the big grocery run until Monday, so the afternoon is open otherwise.
I will text his mom and make sure he has the folder this time.
A few artists are meeting outside city hall before the workshop. I know you usually avoid the megaphone side of things.
I'll come early to set up tables instead. If Don repeats that line about who belongs in the beginner class, I'll ask him who he's picturing.
Good. The room needs to feel open without turning the signup desk into a fight.
I can point to last month's class too. Half the best work came from first-timers he would have overlooked.
I replied under your Arts Council post. The classroom tables need blue tape marks before the watercolor group arrives.
Thanks. I also saw your note about the fiddle duo Friday. I will share that after the supply list.
Good. And at Monday's meeting, let's keep the Main Street parking item to ten minutes.
Agreed. Sign-up sheets first, parking after, then music announcement if we have time.
I printed the sign-up sheet for tomorrow's watercolor workshop. You do not need to remake it tonight.
Good. I was rewriting supply counts and getting short with everybody here.
Then stop at the current version. I'll handle brushes and name tags when I get there.
Deal. I'm going to close the laptop before I convince myself to cancel my part.
Will you still be able to take me to Dr. Henson on Friday mornings if the art room starts needing you?
Yes. I am only considering the blocks that leave that ride alone.
Could you help me with the parish kitchen form after Mass? It asks too many boxes.
I can. I just filled mine out for the council, so the boxes are fresh in my head.
That is a relief. I can move to afternoon if you need me to.
No need. I am not signing onto anything that rearranges church rides or our home evenings.
Thank you. Mine asks for dates from long ago too.
Those are the ones that slow me down. I keep using 05/1976 for birthdate and 1995 for the Van Buren line.
Evan, could you bring the casserole trays by before noon? Only if it doesn't interfere.
I can. I'll combine it with the bank stop and keep the driving short.
Could you help with the parish supper tables this afternoon? We need the tall cart from the closet.
Thank you. Let me give you a little for gas this time.
I can. I'll bring the lace-up boots and use the cart instead of carrying stacks.
I appreciate it. We're keeping errands tight until her next Friday deposit.
That is fine. We can ask Daniel to move the heavy coffee urn.
Thanks. I'll come at 3:15 and do my slow bends before we set the chairs.
Could you take home the extra rolls after setup? I made more than the table needed.
Sure. A half dozen is plenty for our freezer. She will fuss if I bring back three sacks again.
Then I'll send six. Thank her for the foil pans from last time.
Will do. The laundry room shelf is cleared now, so I can stack them there when I get home.
Bring the small binoculars tomorrow if you come. I heard the woodpeckers again near the second bridge.
Still hiking tomorrow, or did the late night with the lights wear you out?
Will do. I also want to try the phone clip on the bend where the bluffs show through.
I'm coming. Just moving slow after helping strike the set and then jumping in for Frank's part.
